Subject: POC trial - next steps & intake: workload profile

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed next steps and kick off the workload intake so our SE/CS teams can size the trial environment and confirm an evaluation plan. Short summary:

- Objective: Run a two-week POC to validate accuracy and latency while exercising ~production traffic patterns for the patient summarization use case.
- Success criteria (what Acme will use to decide):
  * p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 350 ms
  * Quality: summary accuracy >= baseline (we'll run your eval set) with no major regressions
  * Operational: no data leakage, audit logs enabled, and integration with your SSO/KMS
- Timeline proposal: Kickoff week of Aug 31, trial start Sep 1, 2-week evaluation, decision by Sep 18.

Action items I captured:
1) Alice / Raj: share the workload profile below (RPS, token distributions, concurrency, burst patterns) + any PII/PHI flags — reply inline if you can.
2) Ben (SE): propose initial environment (model variant, instance sizing, caching) after intake.
3) Monica (CS): schedule technical kickoff and access requests (service account, IP allowlist).

Attached: trial-matrix.xlsx (blank intake + success criteria table). Please fill the workload row if possible — if not, we can collect during the kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: POC trial - next steps & intake: workload profile

Thanks Alice — quick note from SE perspective to make the intake actionable. Below is the exact information we need to size and recommend a trial configuration. If you can paste values or attach a small CSV that'd be perfect.

Workload / Traffic profile we need:
- Steady-state RPS (requests per second)
- Peak RPS and typical burst length (duration in minutes)
- Typical prompt token length (avg, 90th pct) and typical response token length
- Concurrency: how many concurrent sessions/requests during peak
- Traffic split: % text generation vs % embeddings vs reranking
- Latency SLO (p50/p95 target)
- Example payload sizes (JSON payload, base64 attachments if any)
- Auth & network: will calls originate from a few static IPs or many clients?
- Data sensitivity: any PHI that requires on-prem/VPC deployment?

Initial recommendation (based on similar healthcare trials):
- Start with 4x A40-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) for the first week with autoscale to 8x for burst windows, add KV-cache enabled, and a Gen-1 quantized model family for cost/latency tradeoff.
- We'll enable request-level logging and provide an S3 export of audit logs for compliance review.

I'll put together an environment estimate once we have the numbers. We can also run a short synthetic spike test during kickoff to validate p95 with your payloads.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial - workload intake (numbers)

Thanks Ben — pasted the numbers below from Raj/infra:

- Steady-state RPS: 20 RPS (workloads hitting the summarization endpoint during business hours).
- Peak RPS: 250 RPS typically during morning batch windows; occasional bursts up to ~600 RPS lasting 2–3 minutes during heavy reporting runs.
- Typical prompt tokens: avg 120 tokens, 90th pct 320 tokens.
- Typical response tokens: avg 200 tokens, 90th pct 480 tokens.
- Concurrency: typical concurrent requests 30–40; peak concurrency observed ~150 during bursts.
- Traffic split: ~70% generation (patient summary API), ~25% embeddings (indexing), ~5% reranking.
- Latency SLO: p50 120–150 ms, p95 target 300–350 ms (we can be flexible during the first week).
- Payload size: small JSONs (avg 3–6 KB). Calls originate from ~8 static egress IPs (Raj will provide list).
- Data sensitivity: data will be de-identified but may contain rare PHI fragments. We require SOC2 and audit logs; prefer VPC/private deploy if possible (open to hosted with contract controls if needed).

Also attaching the small scope doc (acme-poc-scopes.pdf) with integration notes and contact list.

Regards,
Alice
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial - workload intake & next steps (confirming owners & timeline)

Appreciate the quick turnaround and great detail — this is exactly what we need. Confirming next steps based on the numbers you provided:

1) Technical kickoff: schedule week of Aug 31. Monica to send calendar invite and access checklist (service account, IP allowlist, SSO test account).
2) Trial environment: Ben will size the initial environment as 4x A40-equivalent with autoscale to 8x for bursts and KV-cache enabled. Ben: please provide a short cost/latency estimate by Monday.
3) Evaluation plan:
  - Week 1 (Sep 1–7): ingest sample dataset, run integration smoke tests, synthetic spike test (simulate 600 RPS for 3 minutes).
  - Week 2 (Sep 8–14): ramp to targeted steady-state and run evaluation against your clinical test set.
  - Decision review by Sep 18.
4) Ownership:
  - Acme: Alice (product lead) and Raj (tech lead)
  - Redwood: Marissa (AE), Ben (SE), Monica (CSM)
5) Compliance: we will surface SOC2 artifacts and enable audit logs. Please confirm if VPC/private deployment is required for the POC or whether hosted with contract safeguards is acceptable.

I've created a shared drive folder and a JIRA ticket for tracking (links below). Monica will follow up with the invite and the blank intake spreadsheet (trial-matrix.xlsx) for any final fields.

Next asks for Acme: please provide the 8 egress IPs and confirm VPC requirement by Mon, Aug 24.

Thanks — I'll coordinate the kickoff scheduling once I see your availability.

—Marissa
